onset.explanation: The earliest qualifying finding is the signed ICE assessment on 02 Jun (Day +5) at 10:55: ICE 9/10, which meets the Grade 1 criterion. The earlier in-window assessments (ICE 10/10 on Day 0 and on 31 May) are formal Grade 0 assessments. The 25 May baseline is outside the observation window (Day -3), so it is not used. The 31 May headache is excluded from grading (§4.2) and does not count. The record onset of 2036-06-02 is the same calendar day as the documented onset.

evidence.quote: ICE assessment on 02 Jun at 10:55: orientation 3/4 (could not give the date), naming 3/3, following commands 1/1, writing 1/1, attention 1/1. Total 9/10.
Neurological screen before infusion: ICE 10/10 at 13:30, alert, no focal deficits.

max_grade.documented_value: 1 or 2 (ambiguous: Grade 2 if the 14:10 ICE 5/10 is accepted, Grade 1 if the 14:40 ICE 8/10 is accepted)
max_grade.explanation: Reason: conflicting assessments (§6.4, A23). On 04 Jun two signed assessments 30 minutes apart disagree. The nurse recorded ICE 5/10 at 14:10 (Grade 2) and the resident recorded ICE 8/10 at 14:40 (Grade 1). Every other assessment is ICE 8, 9 or 10, with no consciousness, seizure, motor or edema criterion met. If the ICE 5 reading is accepted, the maximum is Grade 2, which equals the record (7.7). If the ICE 8 reading is accepted, the maximum is Grade 1, so the record's Grade 2 is unsupported (7.3). The two readings lead to different categories, so the result is 7.5. No competing cause is documented: acetaminophen and tocilizumab are not competing causes.
